statement: >= 20% of announced >100 MW AI data-centre capacity is outside the two leading jurisdictions (Epoch data-centre tracker; IEA; 2027)
status_at_phase_end: No direct measurement in 2024: no public tracker of announced >100 MW AI data-centre capacity by jurisdiction existed (data-gap). Proxies: the IEA's first data-centre electricity analysis (Jan) and a Bloc A national-lab report (Dec) showing fast domestic growth (data centres ~4.4% of Bloc A electricity in 2023, 6.7-12% projected by 2028), consistent with heavy concentration in the two leading jurisdictions. The main sign of diffusion was Bloc A cloud capital entering a Gulf AI firm under an intergovernmental security assurance (Apr) - diffusion under Bloc A control rather than independent capacity.

items.summary: The IEA's annual electricity report included its first in-depth analysis of the data-centre sector's impact on electricity consumption, with forecasts to 2026. Global/regional consumption totals, not a breakdown of announced >100 MW AI sites.
items.detail: IEA, 'Electricity 2024: Analysis and forecast to 2026', 2024-01-24 (CC BY 4.0). Report page verified; specific data-centre figures (e.g. 2022 baseline and 2026 range) not re-read this run, so not quoted.

items.summary: A top-5 Bloc A cloud provider took a USD 1.5 bn minority stake in a Gulf AI company to deliver AI infrastructure across the Middle East, Central Asia and Africa, under a binding intergovernmental assurance agreement. Capacity outside the two leading jurisdictions, but tied to Bloc A security conditions.
items.detail: Microsoft blog, 'Microsoft and G42 partner to accelerate AI innovation in Bloc K and beyond', 2024-04-15 (joint release dated 2024-04-16 in Bloc K).

items.summary: A Bloc A national lab estimated domestic data centres used ~4.4% of national electricity in 2023 and projected 6.7-12% by 2028, with load growth tripled over the past decade and expected to double or triple by 2028. Signals concentration of new capacity in a leading jurisdiction.
items.detail: LBNL, '2024 Report on Bloc A. Data Center Energy Use', announced by Bloc A DOE 2024-12-20 (LBNL news page dated 2025-01-15 adapts the 2024-12-20 DOE release; figures as of the 2024-12-20 release).

items.summary: No public series of announced >100 MW AI data-centre capacity by jurisdiction existed in 2024, so the 20% share cannot be computed for this phase.
items.detail: The Epoch data-centre tracker named in the indicator was not yet public in 2024 (per this project's 2025-phase notes). No source to cite beyond the proxies above.
